Mohan Meah ------ Petitioner 
vs
Dhaka City Corporation represented by its Mayour, Dhaka ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Tariq-ul-Hakim J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed to allot a shop in the first floor of Dhaka New Super Market (south) of Dhaka New Market Complex to the petitioner pursuant to the compromise, Annexures D, E and F recorded in Writ Petition No. 32 of 1987 and Writ Petition No. 372 of 1989 respectively and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. One case namely Writ Petition No. 32 of 1987, filed by Hawkers' Plaza Government Market Baboshayee Samity of which the petitioner claims to be a member, was decreed in compromise between the parties stating, inter alia, that 424 shops will be allotted to the members of the Petitioners' Society on mutual discussion and remaining shops will be allotted by the Dhaka City Corporation as per their discretion. It is alleged by the petitioner that the Dhaka City Corporation did not allot any shop to him despite the aforesaid arrangement and thereafter the said Hawkers' Plaza Government Market Baboshayee Samity and 3 others filed Writ Petition No. 327 of 1989 where on the petitioners' application the Rule was discharged after the parties reached an out of court settlement by which the Dhaka City Corporation agreed to allot shops to 25 persons including the petitioner. The petitioner claims that he is one of the 25 persons and is entitled to get allotment of a shop. The petitioner allegedly made several representations to the Dhaka City Corporation but received no satisfactory response and has therefore been compelled to come to this Hon'ble Court and has obtained the present Rule. 

 9. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the respondents have entered into a compromise with the Hawkers Association of which the petitioner is a member and as per the terms of the compromise which has become part of this Court's decree in Writ Petition No. 32 of 1987, the respondents are under a legal obligation to comply with the terms of the compromise and the refusal of the respondents to allot any shop to the petitioner is illegal and unlawful. It has been further submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the respondents after receiving salami and making an out of Court agreement in Writ Petition No. 372 of 1989 to allot shops to the members of the petitioners Association, the respondents are legally bound to allot a shop to the petitioner. 

 10. As against this, MA Baqui, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1, submits that pursuant to the compromise decree in Writ Petition No. 32 of 1987 424 shops were allotted to the members of the petitioner's Samity but since the name of the petitioner did not appear in the list of members for whom the Samity requested allotment of shops nothing was allotted to the petitioner. He further submits that in the out of Court settlement in Writ Petition No. 372 of 1989 there was no mention of the petitioner and, as such, no shop was allotted to him. He further submits that the petitioner was allotted shop No. D-53 as the Dhaka City Corporation had received salami money from him but the petitioner has refused to accept the same and take possession of the same by paying the balance money. He, therefore, submits that this Writ Petition has got no merit and is liable to be discharged. 

 12. It appears that Dhaka City Corporation allotted 424 shops to the members of the petitioner's Society i.e. Hawker's Plaza Government Market Baboshayee Samity as per compromise decree in Writ Petition No. 32 of 1987. It has been stated that the petitioner was not allotted any shop pursuant to the said agreement since his name was not mentioned in the list of members for whom shops were requested to be allotted by the said Samity to the Corporation. The petitioner's learned Advocate has not been able to satisfy us how he is entitled to get a shop from among those 424 shops and, as such, in our opinion, no illegality has been committed on that count.
